newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha spreads move into backwardation.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha spreads move into backwardation.

text.p: Naphtha's inter-month spreads moved into backwardation for the first time in three months in afternoon Tokyo trade on Thursday, traders said.
The one-month spread from first-half August was quoted at about plus 50 cents, indicating first-half August cargoes were valued 50 cents per tonne higher than first-half September.
Some traders attributed the shift in spreads from contango to backwardation to brisk buying interest from Thailand.
"The supply/demand balance for prompt delivery has started tightening, partly because of spot buying from Thailand," one trader said.
End-users in Thailand were said to have recently bought several full-range cargoes for July and August delivery.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half September was quoted at $201.50/$203.00 per tonne, up by about 50 cents from Wednesday.

Some electric utilities were rumoured to have asked their suppliers to bring forward fuel oil cargo deliveries as a heatwave raised the operating rates of oil-fired power plants. Temperatures in Tokyo exceeded 30 degrees Celsius for seven consecutive days until yesterday.
However, the weather turned mild in Tokyo on Thursday and it was forecast to remain that way for the rest of the week.
